statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-13462: tarfile normalised AREGTYPE blocks to DIRTYPE even while reading the follow-up header of a GNU LONGNAME or LONGLINK member, so a crafted archive could be interpreted differently than by other tools. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/141707 (3.10 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/72dde1016493c52abe857fc4a7bf6c40138b4114), first released in CPython 3.10.21; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-13462. Checked Lib/tarfile.py for the dircheck parameter that skips that normalisation for follow-up headers in the python-3.10 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. Builds before 3.10.20-r2 lack the fix; 3.10.20-r2 and every later build have it (the 3.10.20 builds through a DHI backport). The range ends at 3.10.20-r2.

CVE-2025-13462: the tarfile module still normalized AREGTYPE (\x00) blocks to DIRTYPE while processing a multi-block member such as GNUTYPE_LONGNAME or GNUTYPE_LONGLINK, so a crafted tar archive could be read differently by tarfile than by other implementations. It is fixed on the CPython 3.11 branch by https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/9a23b753552afa28e3a2f4d8863572fc66479406 (https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/141707), first released in CPython 3.11.16. See https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-13462. Checked Lib/tarfile.py for that change in the python-3.11 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.11.14-r0 to 3.11.18-r4 (24 builds), x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. 3.11.14-r0, 3.11.15-r0 and 3.11.15-r1 ship the unmodified tarfile.py of CPython 3.11.14 and 3.11.15, which lacks the fix; 3.11.15-r2 carries a backport of it and every later build carries it, as a backport or from CPython 3.11.16 and later. The range ends at 3.11.15-r2.

CVE-2025-13462: the tarfile module normalized AREGTYPE headers whose name ends in '/' to DIRTYPE even when reading the follow-up header of a GNU long name or PAX member, so a crafted archive could be read differently than by other tar implementations. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/141707 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/ae99fe3a33b43e303a05f012815cef60b611a9c7), first released in CPython 3.13.13; see https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-13462. We read /usr/lib/python3.13/tarfile.py in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package, 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4 (26 builds), on x86_64 and aarch64, after verifying each package against its index checksum: 3.13.12-r0 and 3.13.12-r1 still apply the DIRTYPE normalization to follow-up headers, without the fix; 3.13.13-r1, the first build of CPython 3.13.13, and every later build pass dircheck=False when reading the header after a GNU long name or PAX member, which is the fix.
